headline: Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers have announced approval of the development agreement for the 664-acre Taylor Technology Campus near Austin, Texas, a planned campus of up to one gigawatt that would run on its own natural gas power.
score_reason: The council vote was on 8 Oct 2026 and the story was in our 10 Oct pool; only the companies' announcement is new; lowered 2 from 5.
importance_line: Taylor residents who opposed the project and the city, which now has authority over water use and noise, are most affected, and the on-site gas plant would avoid Texas's long grid-connection queue, but the one gigawatt size is a plan and power is only targeted for 2028.
summary: W.Media reports, citing the companies' press release, that the campus would rely on dedicated gas-fired generation "behind the meter" (connected directly to the site rather than the public grid) with power targeted for the first half of 2028, and that the agreement sets standards on water use, noise, lighting and setbacks. Construction Review reports that Taylor's city council approved the annexation agreement unanimously on 8 Oct 2026 over residents' objections, so the announcement follows that vote.
notes: Follow-up of the 8 Oct council vote (in our 10 Oct pool); W.Media rests on the companies' press release; council-vote detail from Construction Review.
